subject: MAP: acceptance ops checklist & decision anchors
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos@medarishealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: MAP: acceptance ops checklist & decision anchors

Hi Carlos —

Thanks again for a great kickoff yesterday. Attached is the operational acceptance checklist I promised; it nests the MAP milestones with concrete exit gates and suggested acceptance tests so your engineering and procurement teams can validate progress without ambiguity. High-level summary below: 

- Success criteria (what "good" looks like):
  • 95th pct token latency < 250ms for typical clinical prompts (sample set attached)
  • End-to-end throughput to support 10 concurrent clinician sessions at 95% CPU/GPU utilization
  • No PHI leakage in redacted test corpus (privacy tests pass)
  • Model hallucination rate <= 2% on our concordance vignettes

- Exit gates (hard stops):
  1) Security: SOC2 evidence and encryption-in-transit + KMS proof of key access controls
  2) Performance: smoke tests meet latency and throughput thresholds for 3 consecutive runs
  3) Accuracy: concordance acceptance tests meet agreed thresholds (see acceptance-tests-v1.md)

- Acceptance tests: we included a prioritized list (smoke, regression, security) with owners and pass/fail criteria.

Please review the attached MAP_operational_checklist_v1.xlsx — it has the sprint timeline mapped to your EMR integration team and proposed go/no-go dates. If Procurement wants a separate addendum, loop them in and we'll produce a short procurement-specific runbook.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm your preferred pilot start week (we suggested Jan 11–15 in the sheet)?
2) Any additional regulatory evidence your legal/procurement teams will need beyond SOC2?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: MAP_operational_checklist_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 rows)
Attachment: acceptance-tests-v1.md (markdown, 3 sections)

From: Carlos Vega <carlos@medarishealth.com>

Date: 2026-12-15T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: acceptance ops checklist & decision anchors

Neha — thanks for the clear doc. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: the 250ms 95th sounds good, but our clinical UI team wants a soft target at 150ms for the most frequent workflows. Is that realistic in dedicated mode or would that require a different model/quantization profile?
2) Data residency / audit logs: Procurement needs a sample audit log showing per-request metadata and retention window policy; can you point to an example?
3) Acceptance window: Procurement asks for a 2-week acceptance window post-sprint where we'll run the tests and confirm results. Is that acceptable?

Also looping Procurement — can you share any standard procurement appendix/doc showing liability/credits for missed SLAs during pilot?

Regards,
Carlos Vega
Head of Integrations, Medaris Health
carlos@medarishealth.com

Neha / Karthik — drafting replies to Carlos + Procurement. Proposed notes below (I can send if you sign off):

- Latency expectations:
  • 95th pctl <250ms = standard for dedicated pools with the recommended 8-bit quant profile (Q4/8).
  • 150ms 95th is achievable for short prompts + trimmed context on an optimized instance (we should call out increased cost and recommend gating to the 1–2 highest-frequency UI flows). Suggest we add a table of tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs quant).

- Audit logs / data residency:
  • Provide sample logging export (per-request id, timestamp, model_version, token_count, region, request_hash). I'll attach a sanitized sample log and point Procurement to our SOC2 appendix.

- Acceptance window: 2-week acceptance window is reasonable. Recommend these concrete milestones inside that window:
  1) Day 0–3: smoke suite (succeeds)
  2) Day 4–9: focused regression (concordance & PHI-safety tests)
  3) Day 10–14: resilience/stress (throughput) and final sign-off

- Procurement appendix: we have a short SLA credits matrix and pilot liability clause — Ben, can you attach the procurement appendix template?

If that looks good I'll send combined response plus the sample log and updated checklist (I will add the 150ms note and a cost/latency tradeoff table).

—Marissa

Subject: Re: MAP: acceptance ops checklist & decision anchors — updated artifacts and sign-off request

Carlos / Procurement team —

Thanks for the questions; we've updated the artifacts and condensed the plan into a short acceptance runbook. Attachments: MAP_operational_checklist_v1.xlsx (updated), acceptance-tests-v1.md (with owners & explicit pass/fail criteria), sample-audit-log.csv, and procurement-appendix-template.pdf. Key points below so Procurement can quickly review the pilot liability language: 

1) Latency and cost: we added a tradeoff table — 150ms 95th is feasible but only for the two highest-frequency flows using a smaller context window and the performance-optimized instance (estimated +42% monthly pilot cost). We flagged those flows in the checklist so you can decide whether to include them in Pilot v1.

2) Audit logs & residency: sample log attached; retention defaults to 90 days for pilot telemetry. We can extend retention or export on request (we'll note this as an optional procurement appendix item).

3) Acceptance window: we confirm a 2-week acceptance window after the final sprint run. Within that window we require:
   - 3 consecutive smoke runs that meet thresholds
   - Concordance regression under 2% hallucination
   - Security checklist closed with SOC2 evidence cross-reference

4) SLA / credits during pilot: procurement appendix includes a limited-credit schedule tied to uptime and latency SLOs. This is standard for pilot engagements; for production we can discuss expanded remedies.

Next steps:
- Carlos, can you confirm pilot start week (we still have Jan 11–15 suggested)?
- Procurement, if the appendix looks OK we'll prepare DocuSign for the pilot addendum and lock the MAP milestones.

If helpful, I'm available for a 30-min review tomorrow 10–10:30 PT.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
